nodes.summary: If $A x \le b$ is a totally dual integral system with $A$ rational and $b$ integral, then every extreme point of the polyhedron $\{x : A x \le b\}$ is integral. Goemans states the conclusion as "$\{A x \le b\}$ is integral, i.e. all its extreme points are integral"; for a polyhedron without vertices the statement is vacuous. Recorded as wanted.

nodes.summary: For every $b \in \mathbb{R}^n$, the system $x \le b$ (with $A$ the identity matrix) is totally dual integral. nodes.title: Upper-bound systems are totally dual integral

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a real $m \times n$ matrix and $b \in \mathbb{R}^m$. The system $A x \le b$ is *totally dual integral* if for every $c \in \mathbb{Z}^n$ such that the system is feasible and $c^\top x$ is bounded above on $\{x : A x \le b\}$, there are $y \in \mathbb{Z}^m$ with $y \ge 0$ and $A^\top y = c$, and a feasible $x$, with $b^\top y = c^\top x$.
